an4.181:1.1: Endowed with four qualities, monks, a warrior is worthy of a king, an asset to a king, and counts as a very limb of his king.
an4.181:1.3: “There is the case where a warrior is skilled in his stance, able to shoot far, able to fire shots in rapid succession, and able to pierce great objects.
an4.181:1.4: A warrior endowed with these four qualities is worthy of a king, an asset to a king, and counts as a very limb of his king.
an4.181:1.5: “In the same way a monk endowed with four qualities is deserving of gifts, deserving of hospitality, deserving of offerings, deserving of respect, an unexcelled field of merit for the world.
an4.181:1.7: “There is the case where a monk is skilled in his stance, able to shoot far, able to fire shots in rapid succession, and able to pierce great objects. A monk endowed with these four qualities is deserving of gifts, deserving of hospitality, deserving of offerings, deserving of respect, an unexcelled field of merit for the world.
an4.181:2.1: “And how is a monk skilled in his stance?
an4.181:2.2: There is the case where a monk is virtuous. He dwells restrained in accordance with the Pāṭimokkha, consummate in his behavior & sphere of activity. He trains himself, having undertaken the training rules, seeing danger in the slightest faults.
an4.181:2.3: This is how a monk is skilled in his stance.
an4.181:3.1: “And how is a monk one who is able to shoot far?
an4.181:3.2: There is the case where a monk sees any form whatsoever that is past, future, or present; internal or external; blatant or subtle; common or sublime; far or near—every form—as it has come to be with right discernment as: ‘This is not mine. This is not my self. This is not what I am.’
an4.181:3.6: “He sees any consciousness whatsoever that is past, future, or present; internal or external; blatant or subtle, common or sublime, far or near—every consciousness—as it has come to be with right discernment as: ‘This is not mine. This is not my self. This is not what I am.’
an4.181:3.7: “This is how a monk is one who is able to shoot far.
an4.181:4.1: “And how is a monk one who is able to fire shots in rapid succession?
an4.181:4.2: There is the case where a monk discerns, as it has come to be, that ‘This is stress’ … ‘This is the origination of stress’ … ‘This is the cessation of stress’ … ‘This is the path of practice leading to the cessation of stress.’
an4.181:4.3: This is how a monk is one who is able to fire shots in rapid succession.
an4.181:5.1: “And how is a monk one who is able to pierce great objects?
an4.181:5.2: There is the case where a monk pierces right through the great mass of ignorance.
an4.181:5.3: This is how a monk is one who is able to pierce great objects right through.
an4.181:5.4: “Endowed with these four qualities, a monk is deserving of gifts, deserving of hospitality, deserving of offerings, deserving of respect, an unexcelled field of merit for the world.”
